query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount (≈1 wt %) of Ni to a 50 vol % W / 50 vol % Cu powder blend and consolidating it by transient-liquid-phase spark-plasma sintering (TLPS-SPS) at 1180 ± 20 °C under 50 MPa vacuum will create an ultrathin Cu–Ni interdiffusion layer that fully wets W particle surfaces, eliminates >80 % of the residual porosity found in conventional SPS W–Cu, and thereby raises room-temperature bulk thermal conductivity by ≈20 % while retaining ≥90 % of baseline flexural strength after 1000 thermal cycles between 25 °C and 800 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Mechanically alloyed W (d50 ≈ 1 µm) and Cu (d50 ≈ 3 µm) powders premixed to 50 vol % each, no prior compaction; oxygen <300 ppm.
generation.intervention: Introduce 1 wt % Ni uniformly into the Cu powder, then consolidate the W–Cu–Ni blend by spark-plasma sintering with a 50 MPa uniaxial load, heating at 100 °C min⁻¹ to 1180 °C, holding 5 min, followed by furnace cooling.
generation.conditions: Processing in vacuum (<5 Pa) with Ar back-fill on cooling; service envisaged for fusion divertor joint environment, cyclic heating 25–800 °C in high-vacuum or He atmosphere, no oxidizing exposure.
generation.structural_mediator: A transient Ni-rich liquid forms at 1180 °C (above the Cu–Ni eutectic), spreads over W surfaces, fills inter-particle voids, and solidifies into a Cu–Ni solid-solution layer ~50–200 nm thick that promotes metallurgical bonding and eliminates interfacial gaps.
generation.mechanism: The wetting liquid lowers interfacial energy, enabling capillary penetration and pore closure; subsequent Ni diffusion into Cu suppresses permanent liquid phases, so the composite solidifies fully dense. The intimate Cu–Ni/W contact lowers Kapitza resistance and removes phonon/electron scattering at voids, boosting thermal conductivity, while the thin interdiffusion layer avoids the brittle intermetallics that would otherwise degrade strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to baseline SPS-consolidated W–50 vol %Cu without Ni: (i) open porosity falls from ≈5 % to <1 %; (ii) room-temperature bulk thermal conductivity rises from ≈250 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ to >300 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (≈20 % increase); (iii) three-point bending strength remains ≥90 % of baseline (~900 MPa) after 1000 thermal cycles 25–800 °C, indicating preserved mechanical durability.
generation.baseline: Spark-plasma-sintered W–50 vol %Cu composite processed at 1100 °C / 50 MPa / 10 min without Ni addition.
generation.boundary: Composition 40–60 vol % W, 0.3–2 wt % Ni; TLPS-SPS temperature 1150–1200 °C; service in non-oxidizing atmosphere ≤1000 °C. Outside these ranges (e.g., air at >500 °C or Ni >2 wt %), excessive oxidation or brittle phase formation may negate benefits.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of conductivity gain may vary (±10 %) with powder size distribution and Ni homogeneity; long-term neutron irradiation effects on Cu–Ni interlayer stability remain unverified.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of cylindrical samples (φ10 mm × 10 mm): (A) Baseline W–Cu; (B) W–Cu–1 wt %Ni TLPS-SPS processed as specified. Characterize density (Archimedes), microstructure (SEM/EDS, TEM), thermal conductivity (laser-flash diffusivity with calorimetry for Cp), flexural strength (ASTM C1161) before and after 1000 thermal cycles (25↔800 °C, 5 min dwell).
measurements: Thermal conductivity at 25 °C and 800 °C (W m⁻¹ K⁻¹)
Change in properties after thermal cycling (%)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) Sample B shows open porosity >2 %; OR (2) Sample B’s initial thermal conductivity is ≤250 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (≤ baseline) OR <10 % higher than baseline; OR (3) Flexural strength of Sample B after cycling falls below 90 % of baseline value.
